notes: Matched over 3 documents (UMD GenAI guidelines, TLTC sample syllabus language, CS academic-integrity page); stance agreed on all three (delegates, delegates, prohibit). Main disagreements: (1) actor on the administrative-work section: A coded ta-staff, B coded all; resolved from the subject of each sentence (no role named or 'individuals'/'faculty, and staff' -> all). Also instructor vs all for 'faculty, staff, and student-employees', and admin for the designated feedback channel and the Student Conduct evaluation. (2) policy_type: P24 vs P09/P10 for syllabus-content list items (resolved P09), P40 vs P47 for detector disclosure (P47), P59 vs P101 and P48 vs P47 for TA use (P59, P48), P77 vs P65 for procurement, P81 vs P80 for Office of Student Conduct (P80), P84 vs P24 for the document's own AI-editing note (P84), P42 vs P41 (P41), UNCOVERED vs P52 for click-through liability (UNCOVERED), P01 vs UNCOVERED for the stage-limited ban (P01 with fit note). (3) unit_stance: coders disagreed mostly on disclosure/citation units (require/permit vs neutral); resolved neutral because disclosure takes no position on AI use. Prohibit vs restrict resolved from whether the source gives an exception. (4) modality: should vs must (understanding duty -> must; research policies apply -> must; feedback invitation -> may), and informs vs should for the summary instruction line. (5) phase: before-course vs when-misuse for detector advice (before-course), during-work vs before-course for the AI Literacy module (before-course). B-only units (16): 14 kept (scope, expectation to follow guidelines, privacy-office consultation, decline AI meeting tools, administrative policy alignment, investigation privacy, free-tool review, contact office, data classification, sample-template headline and framing, ask-when-unclear); a federal-detector fact recoded UNCOVERED; dropped the approval-date metadata and a future-work clause. A-only units (3): kept the check-the-syllabus student rule and the AI-encouraged sample citation line; dropped the CS page's code-similarity software line (not AI). The matched count excludes the pairing of A's check-the-syllabus line with B's ask-when-unclear line, which are different sentences.
